summary: กองทัพเรือไทยกำลังเฝ้าระวังอย่างหนัก หลังพบกองเรือประมงกัมพูชาที่อาจติดอาวุธกว่า 20-30 ลำ ลุกล้ำเข้ามาในน่านน้ำไทยแถวอ่าวไทย โดยคาดว่าน่าจะเข้ามาลอบขนส่งปลาแซลมอนและสินค้าทะเลกลับไปกัมพูชา ทหารเรือจึงต้องคุมเข้มและลาดตระเวนเพื่อปกป้องอธิปไตยทางทะเลของเรา
title: จับตา! กัมพูชาส่งกองเรือประมงติดอาวุธล่วงล้ำอ่าวไทย ทัพเรือไทยคุมเข้มสกัดลอบขนสินค้า

summary: Business sectors are urging the new Anutin 2 government to reverse the hardline approach that caused nearly 1 million Cambodian workers to flee Thailand since mid-2025. The exodus, driven by nationalist tensions and border conflict, has caused a massive labor shortage that Myanmar and Lao workers cannot fill. The editorial argues that the ban on Cambodian labor hurts Thai businesses and encourages illegal crossings, suggesting that economic security is just as vital as border security.
title: Editorial: Let Cambodian Workers Return to Fix Labor Shortage

summary: Three months after the December ceasefire, Cambodia faces severe economic fallout including the return of 950,000 migrant workers from Thailand and a 37% drop in remittances. While most displaced villagers have left shelters, the closure of land borders by Thailand and the diversification of Thailand's labor force away from Cambodian workers continue to strain Cambodia's economy and test Prime Minister Hun Manet's leadership.
title: After border clashes with Thailand, Cambodia's economic time bomb ticks louder

summary: កម្ពុជាកំពុងសម្របសម្រួលជាមួយក្រុមអ្នកសង្កេតការណ៍អាស៊ាន (AOT) ដើម្បីចុះពិនិត្យមើលស្ថានភាពនៅតាមព្រំដែនតំបន់ភូមិព្រៃចាន់។ ការចុះពិនិត្យនេះធ្វើឡើងស្របពេលដែលថៃបានយកទូកុងតឺណ័រមករារាំង និងរំលោភយកដីខ្មែរជាង 584 ហិកតានៅតំបន់បឹងត្រកួន។
title: កម្ពុជាសម្របសម្រួលក្រុម AOT ចុះពិនិត្យស្ថានភាពព្រំដែន នៅតំបន់ភូមិព្រៃចាន់

summary: กองกำลังบูรพากำลังเร่งเก็บกู้ทุ่นระเบิดแถวชายแดนสระแก้ว บริเวณบ้านหนองจาน ล่าสุดเคลียร์พื้นที่ปลอดภัยไปได้เกือบ 40,000 ตารางเมตรแล้ว และยังขุดเจอระเบิดสังหารบุคคล POMZ-2 ด้วย เจ้าหน้าที่ฝากเตือนชาวบ้านให้ระวังให้ดี เพราะยังมีพื้นที่อันตรายเหลืออยู่อีกตั้งกว่า 60%
title: เร่งกู้ทุ่นระเบิดชายแดนสระแก้ว เผยพื้นที่เสี่ยงยังเหลือกว่า 60,000 ตร.ม.

summary: The ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) visited the Boeung Trakuan border checkpoint in Banteay Meanchey to monitor a fragile ceasefire. Cambodian officials allege the Thai military has blocked road access with barbed wire and shipping containers in the area. The visit coincided with a leadership change in the AOT, as Malaysia handed over its chairing role to the Philippines. Officers from Singapore and Malaysia recently arrived to join the verification mission to ensure both sides adhere to the December 2025 peace agreements.
title: ASEAN Observer Team Visits Boeung Trakuan Border Area Amid Rising Tensions

summary: Cambodia has accused Thailand of violating its sovereignty and reportedly invited a group of diplomats to the Thmodar area (adjacent to Trat province) to inspect Thai military activities, including the raising of flags and the installation of barricades. As of the report, the Thai government has not issued a formal official statement, but the situation is being closely monitored by local media as it could impact bilateral relations.
title: Cambodia Claims Thailand Violated Sovereignty, Takes Diplomats to Thmodar to Inspect Border Barricades

summary: The Royal Thai Army (RTA) has rejected allegations from Phnom Penh that Thai troops are preventing tens of thousands of displaced Cambodians from returning to their homes. RTA spokesman Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree called the claims 'grossly exaggerated,' stating only a few thousand people are affected in Sa Kaeo province. He defended the use of barbed wire and shipping containers as temporary measures to maintain stability following recent clashes, consistent with the December 27 ceasefire.
title: Army denies blocking return of displaced

summary: At 9:33 AM on Sunday, March 29, the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) conducted a mission at the O'Smach International Border Checkpoint in Oddar Meanchey province. Lieutenant General Maly Socheata, spokeswoman for the Ministry of National Defence, stated that the Thai army has illegally occupied part of this area since late December 2025. Specifically, Thai troops are reported to have encroached 420 meters into Cambodian territory. Cambodia reaffirmed its commitment to the 2025 peace agreements and stated its goal is to restore normalcy through the coordination of the ASEAN team.
title: Cambodia Reaffirms Commitment to Border Peace as AOT Monitors Illegal Occupation at O'Smach International Border Checkpoint

summary: The Royal Thai Navy clarified that placing containers and barbed-wire barriers at the border was a response to 'provocation' and the dismantling of original barriers by 'ill-intentioned individuals.' The Navy stated these actions comply with a December 27, 2025, joint statement to maintain current troop positions and are intended to reduce friction between forces rather than infringe on Cambodian sovereignty.
title: Thai Navy says border container move follows Cambodia accord

summary: Local reports from Surin province indicate a temporary calm in border districts like Phanom Dong Rak. Residents who previously fled tensions are returning to normal life, with many parents traveling over 100km to enroll their children in secondary schools. Despite the calm, locals remain concerned about high fuel prices and rumors of potential future clashes after the rainy season.
title: Border quietens down as parents rush to enroll children in famous schools

summary: The Royal Thai Navy addressed Cambodian claims that Thailand's placement of shipping containers and barbed wire along the border violates sovereignty. Rear Admiral Paraj Ratanajaipan stated these are defensive measures prompted by 'ill-intentioned individuals' destroying previous barriers. The Navy claims the placement follows the 2025 Joint Statement to maintain current troop positions and prevent further clashes.
title: Thai Navy insists border containers are for 'self-defense'

summary: Cambodian local media published an analysis alleging that the Thai military-backed government is manufacturing a border defense crisis and initiating an 'illegal invasion of Cambodian territory' to distract the Thai public from its severe domestic economic stagnation, rising household debt, and political instability. The report claims the conflict has displaced over half a million Cambodians and damaged local civilian infrastructure.
title: Price of distraction: Thailand's manufactured hegemony and domestic policy failure reality

summary: The ASEAN-led monitoring mechanism has increased its capacity along the border to ensure the implementation of the peace agreements signed in late 2025. This expansion follows commitments made during the third special meeting of the General Border Committee (GBC) on December 27, 2025. The regional body aims to support a rapid recovery of normalcy and long-term stability between the two neighbors.
title: ASEAN observers expand presence to monitor ceasefire with Thailand

summary: Foreign diplomats and United Nations representatives visited border areas where Cambodian officials allege Thai forces have encroached. Reports indicate Thai troops installed barbed wire and shipping containers in Boeng Trakuon and O'Smach, reportedly moving 420 meters into Cambodian territory following a December ceasefire. The ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) is verifying these developments as leadership of the mission transitions from Malaysia to the Philippines.
title: Foreign envoys, UN reps witness Thai encroachment

source: Bangkok Biz News (กรุงเทพธุรกิจ)
summary: Admiral Phairoj Fuangchan, Commander-in-Chief of the Royal Thai Navy, addressed the ongoing tension at the Thmor Da border in Trat Province. He admitted that Cambodian movements appear to have 'hidden objectives' that Thailand cannot yet clearly evaluate. He emphasized a policy of patience to avoid escalation and confirmed that Thai forces remain strictly behind the 'Troop Deployment Line' (TDL) agreed upon on December 27, 2025. Regarding the use of shipping containers, he stated they are only placed in specific high-risk areas to protect Thai personnel from provocations, such as previous incidents where Cambodian individuals dismantled barbed wire and approached Thai troops.
title: Navy Chief Reveals Cambodia's 'Thmor Da' Provocations Have Hidden Motives, Confirms Container Placement Only in Risky Spots

summary: Thai media reported on footage released by Cambodian sources showing Thai soldiers preventing Cambodian monks and individuals from entering Ta Kwai Temple. The 2nd Army Region of Thailand clarified that the temple remains under Thai supervision and urged citizens not to share photos or videos of military equipment movements for national security. This follows viral claims that Cambodia had retaken the site, which Thai authorities deny, stating they are maintaining their positions according to current security protocols.
title: Cambodian Video Shows Thai Soldiers Blocking Entry to Ta Kwai Temple

summary: High-ranking military officials visited front-line troops to boost morale before the Khmer New Year. Amidst the visit, officials addressed claims regarding the destruction of Khmer temples along the border by Thai forces. The government spokesperson also denied Thai claims that border talks would only happen after the New Year, stating that Cambodia has already submitted five specific requests for negotiation.
title: General Thet Visits Border Forces in Military Region 5 Ahead of Khmer New Year

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation strongly rejected claims that Deputy Prime Minister Prak Sokhonn suggested Cambodia would cede land to Thailand. During a visit to displaced residents in Pursat, Sokhonn stated that Cambodia is committed to peaceful legal mechanisms based on 1904 and 1907 treaties, while accusing Thailand of relying on military power. The ministry clarified that any encroachment found during demarcation must be returned on a reciprocal basis.
title: Cambodia Rejects 'Distorted' Claims of Ceding Land to Thailand

summary: Thai naval authorities removed Captain Thammanoon Wanna, commander of special forces in Trat, and 17 other officers following a heated verbal dispute with Cambodian troops. The conflict began on March 26 at the Thmor Da border crossing over the placement of a Thai flag on a container. A negotiation expert, Colonel Pratchaya Phoyoy, has been appointed to replace him to ease regional tensions and prioritize diplomacy over military force.
title: ថៃដកតំណែងមេបញ្ជាការជើងទឹកម្នាក់ ក្រោយផ្ទុះជម្លោះពាក្យសម្តីជាមួយទាហានកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Thai Navy Commander Removed After Verbal Conflict with Cambodian Soldiers

summary: Three months after the December ceasefire, Cambodia is struggling with the economic fallout of its conflict with Thailand. Approximately 950,000 Cambodian migrant workers returned from Thailand, leading to a massive unemployment shock. The conflict, which displaced over one million people in 2025, has severed critical trade links, with GDP growth projected to slow to 4% in 2026 as the country faces high household debt and energy shocks.
title: After border clashes with Thailand, Cambodia’s economic time bomb ticks louder

summary: The ISEAS daily alert notes a strategic call for Cambodia to establish a 'Thai-Language Strategic Communications Hub.' This initiative aims to address information gaps and communicate Cambodia's perspective directly to the Thai public and international observers, reflecting the ongoing soft-power and diplomatic maneuvering between the two neighbors following recent border friction.
title: Daily News on Southeast Asia – 31 Mar 2026

summary: King Maha Vajiralongkorn has approved the new cabinet for Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul following the February elections. Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow remains in his post as the top diplomat. The new administration, dominated by the Bhumjaithai party, takes office amidst ongoing border tensions and the implementation of a fragile ceasefire with Cambodia brokered in late 2025.
title: Thai King endorses PM Anutin Charnvirakul's new cabinet

summary: The Royal Thai Navy (RTN) responded to reports that Cambodia will receive two Chinese-made Type 056 corvettes, stating they pose no threat to Thailand’s maritime security. Rear Admiral Parach Rattanachaiyaphan highlighted Thailand’s larger fleet and plans to procure high-performance frigates. Meanwhile, the Thai army reported that Cambodian forces had recently withdrawn about one kilometer from positions they previously occupied in the Chong An Ma border area in Ubon Ratchathani.
title: Cambodia warships pose no threat: navy
